# Sources

Read 2026-10-29. One line each: what it is, and what it was used for. Vendor means the publisher sells the thing
it measures.

## Primary data and studies

| Source | URL | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| 30MPC, Gong and Outbound Squad, The Ultimate Cold Email Data Report (2025) | https://tactics.30mpc.com/hubfs/The%20Ultimate%20Cold%20Email%20Data%20Report-1.pdf | 85M+ cold emails. Charts read page by page: length, sentences, personalization types, pitch words, "you" language, CTA types, bump length, breakup language, touches. Vendor (Gong) and trainers. |
| 30MPC newsletter, The data-backed cold email formula | https://www.30mpc.com/newsletter/the-data-backed-cold-email-formula-the-exact-words-length | Text summary of the same report: under 100 words, 3 to 4 sentences, offer types. |
| Gong, How to write a sales email | https://www.gong.io/blog/how-to-write-a-sales-email | 304,174 emails: interest CTA vs time ask; 132,000 emails: ROI language. Also a "longer emails 15x" claim that contradicts its own later report. Vendor. |
| Expandi, State of LinkedIn Outreach H2 2026 | https://expandi.io/state-of-linkedin-outreach-h2-2026/ | 13.2M invitations, 6.7M messages, 13,302 accounts: length brackets, sequence length, openers, AI vs human within accounts, send time. Vendor, observational. |
| Expandi, LinkedIn outreach benchmarks 2026 | https://expandi.io/blog/linkedin-outreach-benchmarks-2026/ | Baselines: 28.5% acceptance, 10.4% message reply, note reply falling 3.5% to 2.2%. Vendor. |
| Belkins, LinkedIn outreach study | https://belkins.io/blog/linkedin-outreach-study | 11.5M invitations (via an automation vendor's campaigns): note 25.3% vs no note 27.6% acceptance; reply 8.2% vs 5.3%. Agency. |
| Reachium, Do connection notes work | https://www.reachium.io/research/do-connection-notes-work | 180,155 invitations, matured cohort; the only source that checks within customers (acceptance gap reverses) and names its confounders. Vendor. |
| Botdog, 16,492 invitations analyzed | https://www.botdog.co/blog-posts/linkedin-acceptance-rates | Acceptance timing (63% within 24 h, 88% within 7 days); note vs blank stated without numbers. Vendor. |
| ReactIn, with or without note, 80K+ | https://www.reactin.io/blog/linkedin-connection-request-with-or-without-note | Ranges only, inconsistent tables, no method. Vendor. |
| Outscore / ConnectionTracker, 7 studies compared | https://www.connectiontracker.org/guides/average-linkedin-connection-acceptance-rate | Table of seven vendor acceptance figures, including Waalaxy 38% vs 26% (no link to source). |
| Prospectio, voice note at step two | https://www.prospectio.ai/data/tests/voice-note-at-step-two/ | Randomized within accounts, 5,915 founders and COOs at 10 to 50 person firms: reply 30.7% to 33.7%, meetings 4.1% to 5.0%; worse in DACH. Vendor. |
| Fuzzy AI, 10,000 LinkedIn messages analyzed | https://getfuzzy.ai/blog/10000-linkedin-outreach-messages-analyzed | Warm (engaged with their post first) 13.1% vs cold 3.1% reply. Vendor, observational. |
| Lavender, Cold email 101 | https://lavender.ai/blog/cold-email-101 | 25 to 50 words, grade 3 to 5 reading level "67% more replies", observation, connection, credibility, question. No sample stated. Vendor. |
| Lavender, Cold email benchmark report | https://lavender.ai/blog/the-cold-email-benchmark-report | 231,818 emails from about 50k inboxes; content insights only in an interactive report. Vendor. |
| Social Media Today, LinkedIn InMail best practices (2022) | https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedin-shares-inmail-best-practices-to-help-maximize-your-response-rates/632108/ | LinkedIn's own line that InMails under 400 characters do best; repeats Lavender's 28.3M email figures. |
| LinkedIn Help, Personalize invitations to connect | https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/46662 | Note up to 200 characters; free accounts: notes on 3 invitations a month; Premium: unlimited. |
| Hublead, LinkedIn character limits 2026 | https://www.hublead.io/linkedin-character-limit | Confirms 200 characters and 3 free notes a month; 300 was the older limit. |
| Reply.io, How to write better cold emails | https://reply.io/wp-content/uploads/How-to-write-better-cold-emails-Reply-Research.pdf | Zero questions +11% reply vs one; three questions down to 21%. Vendor. |
| Hunter, cold email word count | https://hunter.io/blog/cold-email-word-count | 34M cold emails: 20 to 39 words highest reply; critique of the Boomerang question study as warm mail. Vendor. |
| Sahni, Wheeler, Chintagunta 2018, Marketing Science 37(2) | https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:inm:ormksc:v:37:y:2018:i:2:p:236-258 | Field experiments, about 1.2M subscribers: the name in the subject line lifts opens about 20% and leads about 31%. Peer reviewed. |
| Chicago Booth Review on the same paper | https://www.chicagobooth.edu/review/open-name-why-personalized-email-subject-lines-work | Plain summary; effect comes from attention, not information. |
| Jakesch et al. 2019, CHI, AI-mediated communication | https://s.tech.cornell.edu/assets/papers/aimc.pdf | Suspecting text was written by AI lowers how trustworthy the writer seems. Peer reviewed. |
| Hohenstein and Jung 2020, Computers in Human Behavior 106 | https://news.cornell.edu/node/318907 | Smart replies raised trust when unnoticed; the AI took blame when things went wrong. Peer reviewed, 113 students. |
| Fillon et al. 2023, Metapsychology, "But you are free" re-analysis | https://open.lnu.se/index.php/metapsychology/article/view/2640 | 52 studies: g = 0.44 overall, g = 0.11 (not significant) in the 7 low-bias studies. Peer reviewed, preregistered. |
| Carpenter 2013 meta-analysis, "But you are free" | https://drum.lib.umd.edu/handle/1903/24608 | 42 studies, about doubles compliance. Peer reviewed; contested by Fillon. |
| LessWrong review of persuasion evidence | https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/FjrhHEmxEgJXzyBoi/reviewing-the-evidence-on-psychological-manipulation-by-bots | Tiers Cialdini levers: social proof strongest; foot-in-the-door small. Secondary. |
| Foot-in-the-door effect sizes | https://emailanalytics.com/persuasion-techniques/ | r about .17 FITD, .097 door-in-the-face, citing meta-analyses. Secondary. |

## Practitioners (primary where found)

| Source | URL | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Josh Braun, 15 Cold Email Copywriting Principles (PDF) | https://joshbraun.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/15coldemail-copywriting.pdf | Superpowers, expensive problem, make it personal, prospect's words, poke the bear, slow down (interest CTAs list), without, detach (Voss one-liners), end on a high note. Read in full. |
| Josh Braun, Ditch the pitch, poke the bear | https://joshbraun.com/ditch-the-pitch-poke-the-bear/ | Neutral questions on the cost of the current way. |
| Josh Braun, Cold email CTAs | https://joshbraun.com/cold-email-ctas/ | Bad time asks vs good poke-the-bear questions. |
| Becc Holland, How to personalize at scale (PersistIQ repost of the Chorus article) | https://www.persistiq.com/how-to-personalize-at-scale/ | Four "-graphic" principles, five premise buckets in order, three-line structure. |
| Becc Holland, Personalization at Scale deck (Chorus) | https://cdn2.hubspot.net/hubfs/5192515/Customer%20Summit%20Decks/Personalization%20At%20Scale%20-%20Becc%20Holland,%20Chorus.pdf | Premise, then the value mapped onto it, then one ask. |
| Lessons from Becc Holland (Antoine Buteau) | https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-from-becc-holland/ | Personalization vs relevance, why you, why now, follow-ups vary the value, no "just checking in". Secondary. |
| Signum.ai summary of Holland's Chorus playbook | https://medium.com/signum-ai/how-to-build-b2b-outbound-sales-and-do-personalization-at-scale-sales-playbook-from-becc-holland-e00b74e003e7 | 16 steps over 21 business days; 3 premises; heavy and lite touches. Secondary. |
| Justin Michael Method playbook (PDF) | https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5006b364e4b09ef2252d3129/t/632dae8c786ffe1f4650e741/1663938196662/JMM%E2%84%A2+%E2%80%93+Prospecting+Playbook.pdf | The author's own playbook. |
| AiSDR, The Justin Michael Method | https://aisdr.com/blog/email-framework-justin-michael-method/ | Spears, bumps, three clusters, pattern interrupts, checklist. Secondary. |
| Justin Michael on LinkedIn, The JMM | https://www.linkedin.com/posts/michaeljustin_the-justin-michael-method-the-jmm-activity-6923646039899922432-Zn9a | His warning that copied templates decay. |
| Outbound Squad (Jason Bay), podcasts 368, 393, REPLY Method | https://www.outboundsquad.com/podcast/jason-bay2 | Framework named, steps not public in text. |
| Lessons from Morgan Ingram (Antoine Buteau) | https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-from-morgan-ingram/ | Comment before you message, wait a few days after accept, video 10-30-10, low-friction asks. Secondary. |
| Florin Tatulea, Prospecting from the Trenches | https://salesflo.substack.com/ | Newsletter; frameworks paywalled; nothing citable found. |
| Regie, 3x3 research | https://www.regie.ai/blog/3-x-3-research-101 | Credits 3x3 (three facts in three minutes) to Steve Richard of Vorsight, not Jason Bay. |
| Chris Voss, calibrated questions (Shortform summary) | https://www.shortform.com/blog/what-is-a-calibrated-question/ | What and how questions, avoid why. Secondary to Never Split the Difference (2016). |
| Close, cold email tips from 20 sales leaders | https://close.com/blog/cold-email-tips-linkedin | Mentions Kyle Coleman's critique of a cold email; his rules not reachable. |
| Growth Unhinged, Sam McKenna frameworks | https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/sales-frameworks-sam-mckenna | Paywalled; Show Me You Know Me only via summaries. |
| 30MPC podcast 596, Sam McKenna | https://podcastrex.com/shows/30-minutes-to-presidents-club-no-nonsense-sales/596-this-cold-email-formula-gets-20-replies-exact-templates/transcript | Her test: a subject line that would make sense to nobody else. |

## Frameworks and copywriting history

| Source | URL | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| E. St. Elmo Lewis (AIDA) | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._St._Elmo_Lewis | Usual attribution of AIDA, 1898. |
| Journal of Marketing and Historical Research, AIDA origin | https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jmhr/3/2/3_150/_article/-char/ja | Disputes the Lewis attribution (credits Sheldon, Dukesmith). Abstract only. |
| Copyblogger, The four P approach | https://copyblogger.com/4ps/ | Promise, Picture, Proof, Push. |
| GMass, Promise Picture Proof Push | https://www.gmass.co/blog/promise-picture-proof-push/ | Order varies; attribution to Henry Hoke Sr. is secondhand. |
| GMass, Star Story Solution | https://www.gmass.co/blog/star-story-solution/ | The formula; no origin. |
| Saleshandy, 10 cold email frameworks | https://www.saleshandy.com/blog/cold-email-frameworks/ | QVC, PPP, BAB definitions. No origins. |
| The Personal MBA, levels of awareness | https://personalmba.com/levels-of-awareness/ | Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (1966), five levels. |
